fields.label: What
fields.description: What it is, in the words somebody would use asking about it — “Utah contractor licence”, “General liability”, “Workers' comp policy”.

fields.label: Kind
fields.options:
Licence
Insurance
Registration
Permit
Audit
Other
fields.description: “Audit” is here because the workers' comp premium audit is a deadline with no certificate behind it, and a register that only holds documents misses exactly that kind.

fields.label: Number
fields.description: Policy or licence number — the thing a customer asks for.

fields.label: Whose job
fields.description: A plain name or role, not a Link. Same rule as the checklists: a required assignee is how a register stops being kept up.

fields.label: Expires
fields.description: The whole point of the record. Required, because a row with no date is a row the sweep cannot warn about and nobody looks at.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: DERIVED nightly from the date. The same four words the credential register uses, because two expiry models that disagree about what “Expiring” means is worse than either alone.

fields.label: Warn this many days ahead
fields.description: A contractor licence renewal takes weeks; a vehicle registration takes a morning. One horizon for both would be wrong for one of them.

fields.label: The document
fields.description: The certificate a customer asks for. Attached here so the answer to “can you send us your COI” is one click rather than a search of somebody's inbox.

fields.label: Subcontractor
fields.description: Set when this is somebody ELSE'S certificate that we hold — a subcontractor's COI. Their lapse is our exposure, and it is the one nobody is watching.
